questions.question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.

impossible or extremely difficult to understand
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. **incomprehensible**.

**incomprehensible**- not able to be understood; not intelligible.

**inaudible**- unable to be heard.

**incompatible**- (of two things) so different in nature as to be incapable of coexisting.

**inevitable**- certain to happen; unavoidable.

Option one conveys the meaning of the written group of words.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

ADHERE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 3 i.e. **comply**.

**ADHERE**- stick fast to (a surface or substance).

**ignore**- refuse to take notice of or acknowledge; disregard intentionally.

**detach**- disengage (something or part of something) and remove it.

**comply**- act in accordance with a wish or command.

**release**- allow or enable to escape from confinement; set free.

Option 3 best expresses the meaning of the given word.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The shopkeeper asked me, "Where is your car?"

options.text: The shopkeeper asked me where was my car.
The shopkeeper asked me where my car is.
The shopkeeper asked me where is your car.
The shopkeeper asked me where my car was.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

We have to write the sentence in indirect case always in assertive for and the only option 2 and 4 have this structure.

We need to change the tense into past form.

Both conditions are fulfilled by option 4 so the chosen option is correct.

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Billionaire Philip is the owner of the luxury yacht Lionheart, which worth an estimated $150 million.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• The verb 'is' is missing after 'which'. 
 
• **Therefore, the correct sentence is** 'Billionaire Philip is the owner of the luxury yacht Lionheart, which **is **worth an estimated $150 million'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

INORDINATE
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• The meaning of the given words:
 
• Inordinate: Excessive, unreasonable or inappropriate in magnitude; extreme.
 
• Exorbitant: Exceeding proper limits; extravagant.
 
• Reasonable: Just, fair, agreeable to reason.
 
• Undue: Excessive, unjustified.
 
• Extreme: in the greatest or highest degree.
 
• **Therefore, 'reasonable' is the antonym of the given word.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

CURRENT
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• The meaning of the given words:
 
• **Current: existing or occurring at the moment.**
 
• **Present: Relating to now, for the time being; current.**
 
• Antiquated: Old-fashioned; out of date.
 
• Old: of an earlier time.
 
• Uncommon: Rare, not readily found; unusual.
 
• **Therefore, out of given options, 'present' is the best alternative of the given word.**

questions.question:

sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

The boys were delighted __on the idea of __going to Goa.
questions.solution:

• The correct preposition to be used here is 'at' which is used to indicate an activity. Article 'the' should be used because the specific reason is mentioned why the boys were delighted.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sequence is followed by Option 1.**

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **in.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

The meaning of the given prepositions: 

 
• 'By' is used as a preposition of place- it means “beside” / “at the side of” / “next to”. It also means 'with the help of'
 
• **'In' is used for unspecific times during a day, month, season, year.**
 
• 'At' is used to indicate location or arrival in a particular place or position
 
• 'On' is used to indicate the contact or a surface of something.
 
• **Therefore, in this passage as we are mentioning a year, the suitable preposition is 'in'.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

JEOPARDIZE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. **protect**.

**JEOPARDIZE**- put (someone or something) into a situation in which there is a danger of loss, harm, or failure.

**hazard**- a danger or risk.

**protect**- keep safe from harm or injury.

**threaten**- state one's intention to take hostile action against (someone) in retribution for something done or not done.

**imperil**- put at risk of being harmed, injured, or destroyed.

Only option 2 expresses the opposite meaning of the given word.

questions.question:

He tried to prevent his friend __to smoke.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. from smoking.

The word prevent is always followed by **FROM + V4**.

This is in the option 4 so, the chosen option is correct.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The Japanese Emperor Akihito abdicated the Chrysanthemum Throne in April, 2019.

options.text: The Chrysanthemum Throne was abdicated by the Japanese Emperor Akihito in April,2019.
The Chrysanthemum Throne is abdicated by the Japanese Emperor Akihito in April,2019.
The Chrysanthemum Throne has abdicated by the Japanese Emperor Akihito in April,2019.
The Japanese Emperor Akihito was abdicated by the Chrysanthemum Throne in April, 2019.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

As sentence is in simple past tense ( **subject + v2** ) we need to change it into ( **was/were + v3** ).

This is only in option 1 so, the chosen option is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Municipal corporations have started to take ______ of the problems of waste management.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (1)** i.e. '**cognizance'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• In this context, it is said that " the municipal corporations have begun to recognize and acknowledge the issues related to waste management."
 
 
• **cognizance**- knowledge or awareness. (किसी चीज़ का पूर्ण ज्ञान, संज्ञान)

 
 
• **For example: **The manager took ***cognizance*** of the employee's hard work and dedication.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the complete sentence is *"Municipal corporations have started to take cognizance __of the problems of waste management."*
